facts.title: The makers confirm the vector is real and lethal
facts.text: The Cradlekeepers' own assay decks record the moment a containment trial failed and the engineered strain proved it could rewrite a body from the marrow out. It is the proof the colony will later need that this is no ruin to autopsy.

facts.title: The makers name what they are fighting
facts.text: The host-line that would become the Stillborn Host catalogs the strain's nature: it travels first through read meaning, then through flesh. Naming it is the only reason a seal was ever conceivable.

facts.title: The makers learn what holds it asleep
facts.text: In the salt vaults the makers find that dormancy-salt and a held cold-glyph keep the vector under. They learn the exact condition a seal must hold and, with it, the exact mistake that wakes the thing.

facts.title: The makers cast the keystone the seal was built around
facts.text: A single load-bearing relic is forged to anchor the whole containment lattice. The Cradlekeepers build everything else around it, then run out of time before they can set it.

facts.title: The makers seal themselves into quarantine-sleep beside the thing that hunted them
facts.text: With the seal unfinished, the Cradlekeepers chose dormancy over death: they sealed into the salt vaults alongside the carriers they could no longer separate from their own, gambling that someone would one day read the beacons and finish the lattice. This is the moment the whole world hinges on, the seal that was never finished.

the load-bearing piece the makers' lattice was cast around and never set; inert alone, decisive in sequence
the makers' own ordered protocol for assembling the seal, written so the steps cannot be done out of order without reseeding the strain
opens a salt vault; whether the sleeper inside wakes as a maker who knows the recipe or as a carrier depends on reading the cold-glyph first

facts.text: The makers' record proves the extinction-vector is real, self-replicating and lethal, and that they SEALED rather than died. There is no corpse-civ here; there are sleepers and a clock.

The assay identifies this world's strain as a biological-memetic pathogen that spreads first through the meaning of a read relic and then through the marrow, so any seal must hold both lore and bodies.
The cold-glyph reveals exactly what keeps the vector asleep, naming the condition the seal must hold and the single misreading that wakes a carrier.
The keystone is located: the load-bearing relic the makers' lattice was cast around and abandoned, useless until the prior steps are in hand.
With proof, nature, trigger and keystone in hand and in order, the seal assembles and finishes the containment the makers never closed, after which a vault can finally be opened safely.

facts.present_stakes: the sleeper on drift-carrier-ninth is stirring as its dormancy-salt fails, and threshold-landing sits inside its range; the makers' half-finished seal is the only thing that can hold it
facts.win_condition: read the recipe and assemble the seal in order (proof -> identify -> trigger -> keystone -> assemble) before the carrier fully wakes, after which a maker can be woken safely as an ally
facts.fail_state: cracking a relic out of order or opening the host-vault before the cold-glyph is read reseeds the strain inside the colony NOW or wakes the Stillborn Host carrier; extinction by the colonists' own hand
facts.next_beat_trigger: Devrant's out-of-order crack of the marrow-assay starts showing in the foam fields, forcing Mara to choose between quarantining him and losing a runner mid-race
facts.next_beat_stakes: if the cold-glyph is not read before Soren opens the host-vault, the woken sleeper is a carrier and the dome breaches
facts.note: a forward containment protocol racing a present sleeping threat, not an autopsy of how the makers fell
